notes: USGS-published, not yet served by NSS/StreamStats (status awaiting_nss): Kohn, Mast and Gross, SIR 2025-5047 (published 2026; pubs page revised 2026-05-18). NSS still serves the 2009/2016/2006 equations in CO.json (citations 20, 21, 11); load this set with load_state('CO', allow_awaiting_nss=True). NSS holds the report as a staging draft, citation 200 ('2023, Peak-, Mean-, and Low-Streamflow ... 2019', placeholder URL), regression regions 995-998, status 2 'Review' (disabled for public NSS and StreamStats users, enabled on test.streamstats.usgs.gov); checked 2026-10-13. Keying: by the maintainer's decision the set is stored as NSS staging citation 200 has it, so that StreamStats basin characteristics feed it directly once NSS approves it: NSS's variable codes, units and limits, and NSS's region bounds. The coefficients, intercepts, SEP, SME and N are Table 1's (pp. 20-22), and NSS's staging equation strings match them term for term. Variable codes (report Table 1 code -> stored NSS code): AREA DRNAREA -> DRNAREA (mi2, log10); LONG LONG_CENT -> LONG_CENT (basin-centroid longitude, decimal degrees NAD 83, negative west); SLOPE BSLDEM10M -> ALTBSLDEM ('Alternate mean basin slope', percent); MEANELEV ELEV -> ALTELEV ('Alternate mean basin elevation', ft NAVD 88); SWE APR1_SWE -> APR1_SWE (mean April 1 snow-water equivalent, inches, as NSS and Table 1's range 0-33.8 have it; Table 1.2 lists the SNODAS April 1 SWE in meters); P100Y24H/100Y24H I24H100Y -> ALI24H100Y ('Alternate 24-hour, 100-year rainfall', in.; the Sub-Alpine rows print P100Y24H and the Plateau rows 100Y24H for the one variable the headnote defines); PPTANN PRECIP -> PRECPRIS10 (mean annual precipitation, PRISM 1981-2010, in.). All but DRNAREA enter untransformed (identity), as printed: Q = 10^b0 AREA^b1 10^(c1*X1 + c2*X2 [+ c3*X3]) (eq. 5). The top-level variable_codes map records the same correspondence. Limits are NSS's, which are the pooled ranges of Table 1's headnote at full precision: Table 1 prints AREA 0.22-22,629 mi2, LONG -110.219 to -105.093, SLOPE 3.37-69.4, MEANELEV 4,808-11,954, SWE 0-33.8, 100Y24H 2.19-5.21 and PPTANN 7.71-61.6; NSS has 0.22-22629, -110.218802642652 to -105.093183176045, 3.37-69.38562279, 4808-11954, 0-33.8, 2.1935174416934-5.21209717237366 and 7.71-61.6. No per-region ranges are published. Table 1.1's per-gage drainage areas span Alpine 0.89-1,310, Sub-Alpine 0.76-1,450, Mid-Elevation 1.79-17,100 and Plateau 0.22-22,600 mi2 (five Alpine/Sub-Alpine gages list #N/A), so the pooled 22,629 mi2 maximum is far outside the Alpine and Sub-Alpine fits and extrapolation warnings will not catch that. Region selection (the caller's job; the library does not select regions) is by mean basin elevation, ALTELEV, with NSS's gap-free bounds, recorded per region in region_selection and in region_name: Alpine ALTELEV >= 10490; SubAlpine 9492 <= ALTELEV < 10490; MidElevation 8014 <= ALTELEV < 9492; Plateau ALTELEV < 8014 (NSS's description of the Plateau limitation says 'less than 9014', a typo for its criteria string 'ALTELEV<8014'). The report's own bounds (Table 1 headnote and p. 9) are Alpine > 10,490; Sub-Alpine 9,493-10,490; Mid-Elevation 8,015-9,492; Plateau < 8,014 ft, which leave 1-ft gaps and put exactly 10,490 ft in Sub-Alpine rather than Alpine. Gages: 105, 104, 104 and 105 (418 through WY2019), none used in two regions. Error statistics: sep_log is Table 1's SEP (percent, the square root of the mean GLS variance of prediction, p. 13) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); NSS returns the same SEP as ASEp. model_error_variance is the SME (percent) converted the same way and squared, the CO.json convention. No covariance matrix or per-site AVP is published; the report puts the final models in its data release (doi:10.5066/P9Q5AMFV), which is 'Under Revision' and unavailable as of 2026-10-13, so intervals fall back to sep_log. pseudo-R2 is not stored. Not stored: Tables 2-5 (mean-annual, mean-monthly, 7-day minimum and maximum, flow-duration) and Table 6 (drainage-area-ratio exponents). For a basin in two regions the report weights the flows, not their logs, by area fraction (p. 32): evaluate_weighted(..., space='linear'). Double entry: values were parsed from the report's JATS XML (MathML) and checked against an independent parse of the PDF text layer (intercepts, coefficients, N, pseudo-R2 and SEP for all 32 equations, and the SME column in order) with zero disagreements, and are typed a third time in tests/test_regression_colorado_2025.py, which also reproduces NSS staging Estimate values (3 significant figures) at two input sets per region.
